name: VideoRSI
description: Recursively improves a video SFT data pipeline rather than model weights. Source videos are split into chronological 60-second chunks, captioned, and turned into a timestamped evidence store of entities and events. Grounded multiple-choice tasks are mined from that store, refined, and filtered by schema validity, text-only solvability, frozen-target difficulty, and deduplication. After each iteration, candidate yield, validation failures, and accepted frontier-and-novel counts are used to update task definitions, prompts, operators, and pipeline routing. The target model is not trained during pipeline search. The reported run used five iterations and synthesised a 4.5k video SFT set.
feedback_signal: Pipeline-search diagnostics collected each iteration: candidate yield, evidence and schema validation, text-only checks, frozen-target difficulty, duplicate rejection, and accepted frontier-and-novel samples under a fixed budget. These signals update task definitions, prompts, operators, and routing. The target model is not repeatedly trained during the search, and Video-MME scores are reported after the fact rather than used as the in-loop acceptance rule.
stopping_rule: Fixed budget of five pipeline iterations. No convergence or early-stopping criterion. The final best pipeline synthesises the SFT set; the target model is trained only after pipeline search ends.
